title: "Advanced Mathematics for ICPC"
subtitle: "A dependency-guided course for experienced competitive programmers"
toc: true
---

Build the recognition, derivation, and modelling skills behind hard
competitive-programming mathematics. The course assumes you already have a
tested implementation library and focuses on deciding **what** to apply and
**why** it works.

[Start with the prerequisite audit](00-prerequisite-audit/chapter.qmd) or
[open the study plan](STUDY_PLAN.qmd).

This is a dependency-guided course for an experienced competitive programmer who
already solves around Codeforces 2200 level.  It is deliberately biased toward
techniques that turn a difficult mathematical observation into an implementable
algorithm.  Geometry is out of scope.

The notes assume that the reader already has a comprehensive, tested algorithm
library. They focus on contracts, derivations, recognition clues, and failure
modes rather than reproducing standard implementations. Code appears only when
a non-standard snippet materially clarifies an idea. Shared symbols and preconditions are collected in
[notation reference](NOTATION.qmd).

## How to use the course

1. Take the [prerequisite audit](00-prerequisite-audit/chapter.qmd). Patch only
   the gaps it exposes.
2. Read a chapter's theory before opening its problem hints.
3. Attempt each problem for 60--120 minutes.  Open Hint 1 only when you cannot
   name the relevant mathematical object; open Hint 2 only when the reduction
   remains unclear; use Hint 3 when you know the mathematics but cannot obtain
   the target complexity.
4. After solving, write a three-line postmortem: recognition clue, decisive
   identity, and the implementation hazard you would miss next time.
5. Re-solve Mastery and Capstone problems after two and six weeks.

For a concrete multi-month cadence, use the optional
[24-week study plan](STUDY_PLAN.qmd).

Problem levels used throughout the repository are local to this course:

- **Foundation** isolates one prerequisite or modelling step.
- **Advanced** combines a central theorem with a standard algorithm.
- **Mastery** hides the model or requires a non-obvious transformation.
- **Capstone** combines several chapters or is appropriate team-contest work.

## Dependency map

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  audit[00 · Audit] --> mod[01 · Modular algebra]
  audit --> comb[04 · Combinatorics]
  audit --> lin[10 · Linear algebra]
  audit --> sums[12 · Discrete sums]
  mod --> nt[02 · Multiplicative NT] --> sieve[03 · Advanced sieves]
  comb --> groups[05 · Group actions]
  comb --> poly[06 · Polynomials] --> fps[07 · Formal power series]
  poly --> gf[08 · Generating functions]
  fps --> gf
  audit --> trans[09 · Transforms] --> poly
  lin --> prob[11 · Probability]
  sieve --> core[13 · Core capstones]
  groups --> core
  gf --> core
  prob --> core
  sums --> core

  mod --> mc[14 · Modular combinatorics]
  comb --> mc
  mod --> ffp[15 · Finite-field polynomials]
  poly --> ffp
  comb --> sps[16 · Set power series]
  trans --> sps
  lin --> alggraph[17 · Algebraic graph methods]
  ffp --> alggraph
  gf --> holo[18 · Holonomic methods]
  lin --> holo
  mc --> frontier[19 · Frontier capstones]
  sps --> frontier
  alggraph --> frontier
  holo --> frontier
```

The arrows are deliberately conservative.  For example, probability can be
studied before linear algebra if you postpone absorbing Markov chains, and
Burnside can be studied before all of advanced combinatorics.

## Recommended track

| Phase | Chapters | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| A. Algebraic base | [01](01-modular-algebra/chapter.qmd), [04](04-combinatorics/chapter.qmd) | Move fluently between congruences, fields, identities, and counting models. |
| B. Core engines | [02](02-multiplicative-number-theory/chapter.qmd), [06](06-polynomials/chapter.qmd), [10](10-linear-algebra/chapter.qmd) | Understand the contracts and structure of reusable algebraic machinery. |
| C. Inversion viewpoints | [05](05-group-actions/chapter.qmd), [09](09-transforms/chapter.qmd), [12](12-discrete-sums/chapter.qmd) | Recognize symmetry, poset inversion, and summation transformations. |
| D. Advanced coefficient work | [07](07-formal-power-series/chapter.qmd), [08](08-generating-functions/chapter.qmd) | Derive and compute difficult coefficients, including Lagrange inversion. |
| E. Large-domain and stochastic work | [03](03-advanced-sieves/chapter.qmd), [11](11-probability/chapter.qmd) | Handle summatory functions and expectation systems at contest scale. |
| F. Synthesis | [13](13-capstones/chapter.qmd) | Solve mixed, team-contest-strength mathematics. |
| G. Frontier algebra | [14](14-modular-combinatorics/chapter.qmd), [15](15-finite-field-polynomials/chapter.qmd), [16](16-set-power-series/chapter.qmd) | Work beyond ordinary factorials, univariate FPS, and basic subset transforms. |
| H. Frontier synthesis | [17](17-algebraic-graph-methods/chapter.qmd), [18](18-holonomic-methods/chapter.qmd), [19](19-frontier-capstones/chapter.qmd) | Apply randomized polynomial models and polynomial-coefficient recurrences. |

Within a phase, follow the order in each chapter and its practice page. A
chapter's practice list is ordered; contest rating is only a secondary signal.

## Chapter index

| # | Chapter | Core ideas |
|---:|---|---|
| 00 | [Prerequisite audit](00-prerequisite-audit/chapter.qmd) | Diagnose rather than relearn routine material. |
| 01 | [Modular algebra](01-modular-algebra/chapter.qmd) | Finite fields, CRT, valuations, roots, discrete logarithms. |
| 02 | [Multiplicative number theory](02-multiplicative-number-theory/chapter.qmd) | Factorization, multiplicative functions, Möbius and Dirichlet inversion. |
| 03 | [Advanced sieves](03-advanced-sieves/chapter.qmd) | Quotient blocks, Du Jiao, Min_25, powerful-number enumeration. |
| 04 | [Combinatorics](04-combinatorics/chapter.qmd) | Inclusion--exclusion, classical families, transforms and interpretations. |
| 05 | [Group actions](05-group-actions/chapter.qmd) | Burnside and Pólya enumeration. |
| 06 | [Polynomials](06-polynomials/chapter.qmd) | NTT/FFT, arbitrary-mod convolution, evaluation and interpolation. |
| 07 | [Formal power series](07-formal-power-series/chapter.qmd) | Newton iteration, exp/log/pow/sqrt, composition and reversion. |
| 08 | [Generating functions](08-generating-functions/chapter.qmd) | OGF/EGF models, recurrences, Bostan--Mori, Lagrange inversion. |
| 09 | [Transforms](09-transforms/chapter.qmd) | Poset zeta/Möbius, FWT, subset and divisor convolutions. |
| 10 | [Linear algebra](10-linear-algebra/chapter.qmd) | Elimination, determinants, Kirchhoff, recurrences and black-box methods. |
| 11 | [Probability](11-probability/chapter.qmd) | Indicators, conditional expectation, stochastic DP and Markov systems. |
| 12 | [Discrete sums](12-discrete-sums/chapter.qmd) | Differences, floor sums, continued fractions and Diophantine tools. |
| 13 | [Mixed capstones](13-capstones/chapter.qmd) | Problems that require choosing and combining several tools. |
| 14 | [Modular combinatorics](14-modular-combinatorics/chapter.qmd) | Lucas/Kummer, prime-power binomials, q-analogues. |
| 15 | [Finite-field polynomials](15-finite-field-polynomials/chapter.qmd) | Square-free decomposition, Frobenius, Berlekamp and Cantor–Zassenhaus. |
| 16 | [Set power series](16-set-power-series/chapter.qmd) | Subset convolution, exp/log, composition and power projection. |
| 17 | [Algebraic graph methods](17-algebraic-graph-methods/chapter.qmd) | Pfaffians, Tutte matrices, polynomial identity testing. |
| 18 | [Holonomic methods](18-holonomic-methods/chapter.qmd) | D-finite series, P-recursive sequences, guessing and certification. |
| 19 | [Frontier capstones](19-frontier-capstones/chapter.qmd) | Tag-free synthesis of the extension material. |

## Source and spoiler policy

Statements are linked, not copied.  The notes paraphrase the mathematical idea
and give layered hints rather than complete solutions to listed exercises.
Official statements and editorials are preferred; high-quality community
tutorials are used where they explain a theorem better.  A language label is
shown when a useful source is not English. See [the sources page](SOURCES.qmd) for the
source hierarchy and durable reference material.

No collection can guarantee that a future ICPC problem will not introduce new
mathematics.  The goal here is stronger and more realistic: build the common
toolkit, the habit of deriving missing variants, and enough hard practice that a
new statement can be reduced to familiar algebra under contest pressure.
